message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points (2024)** | Topic | Summary | Practical Tips | |-------|---------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits: 35–55 mph on rural roads, 45–65 mph on highways, 25–35 mph in residential zones.
• “No speed limit” roads (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have a default 70 mph limit unless posted otherwise. | • Always obey posted signs; use a GPS that updates speed limits. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety Seat** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster. | • Check the seat‑belt sign on the dashboard; it turns green when all occupants are buckled. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held texting or calling while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | • Use voice‑activated features or a Bluetooth headset. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑abuse treatment, possible jail time. | • If you’re a passenger, offer to drive or call a rideshare. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians always have priority at crosswalks. | • Yield to pedestrians and cyclists; use caution at school zones. | | **School Bus** | • Stop on both sides of the road when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• The stop sign is active for 30 seconds after the bus stops. | • Do not drive past a stopped school bus until the stop sign is removed. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Use turn signals at least 100 ft before changing lanes.
• Do not pass on the right unless the left lane is occupied by a slow vehicle. | • Keep a safe following distance (at least 2–3 seconds). | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are allowed only when visibility is less than 200 ft. | • Clean your windshield and mirrors regularly. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker on the rear window.
• Towing a vehicle requires a proper tow bar and a towing permit if the vehicle is not registered. | • Keep your registration documents in the glove compartment. | | **Parking** | • No parking on sidewalks, in front of driveways, or in fire lanes.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid handicap placard. | • Pay attention to street‑cleaning signs and meter times. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Speed cameras are installed on many highways; fines are automatically issued. | • Drive within posted limits; avoid “speed traps.” | | **Electronic Toll Collection (TxTag)** | • TxTag is required on toll roads like the 335, 130, and 45. | • Install a TxTag or use the toll‑by‑plate system; otherwise, you’ll receive a bill. | | **Winter & Snow Conditions** | • Texas rarely has snow, but icy patches can occur.
• Use winter tires or chains if required by local ordinances. | • Reduce speed and increase following distance in slick conditions. | ### Quick Reference Resources - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official traffic rules, maps, and updates. - **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text (available online). - **Texas DMV** – Licensing, registration, and driver‑education materials. - **Local County Courts** – For specific traffic violation penalties and court dates. --- #### How to Stay Informed 1. **Download the TxDOT app** – real‑time traffic alerts and speed limit updates. 2. **Subscribe to the Texas DMV email alerts** – for changes in licensing laws. 3. **Check local news outlets** – for updates on road construction or new traffic camera installations. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law, penalty, or how to handle a particular traffic situation in Texas!
